'''Emcure Pharmaceuticals Limited (Emcure)''' is an Indian multinational [[Pharmaceutical industry|pharmaceutical]] company, headquartered in [[Pune]]. Emcure's product portfolio includes [[Tablet (pharmacy)|tablets]], [[Capsule (pharmacy)|capsules]] (both [[softgel]] capsules and hard-gel capsules) and injectables.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Emcure Pharmaceuticals {{!}} Leading Global Pharmaceutical Company|url=https://www.emcure.com/|access-date=2021-08-23|website=Emcure|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Emcure Pharmaceuticals|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/topic/Emcure-Pharmaceuticals|access-date=2021-08-23|website=The Economic Times}}</ref> The company produces [[gynaecology]], [[cardiovascular]], [[oncology]] and [[blood]] [[therapeutic drugs]], [[HIV]] [[Antiviral drug|antivirals]] and other [[Infection prevention and control|anti-infectives]], and [[Dietary supplement|vitamins and minerals]].<ref name="Revenue"/><ref>{{cite web |title=Emcure Pharmaceuticals Ltd |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/profile/company/763195Z:IN |website=Bloomberg |access-date=28 June 2024}}</ref>

== History ==
Emcure Pharmaceuticals was established in 1981 by Satish Mehta, who began the company with a bank loan of {{INR}}3 [[lakh]] (about US$35,000 then) after graduating from [[Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad|IIM-A]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Thakur |first1=Gaurav |title=A cure from Mr Mehta |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/pune-times/a-cure-from-mr-mehta/articleshow/254639.cms |access-date=3 July 2024 |work=The Times of India |date=28 October 2003}}</ref> In the 1990s, the company transitioned from being a [[contract manufacturing organization]] to a producer of [[generic drug]]s.<ref>{{cite web |title=Satish Mehta & family |url=https://www.forbes.com/profile/satish-mehta-1/ |website=Forbes |access-date=10 July 2024 |language=en}}</ref>

In 2006, Emcure signed license agreements with [[Bristol-Myers Squibb]] for [[Atazanavir]]<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/Companies/Bristol-Myers-outsources-AIDS-drug-to-Emcure-106021701143_1.html|title=Bristol-Myers outsources AIDS drug to Emcure|publisher=Business Standard| newspaper=Business Standard India |date=17 February 2006}}</ref> and [[Gilead Sciences]] for [[Tenofovir]] as part of their Global Access Programs.<ref>{{cite news |title=Gilead Sciences in pact with drug trio |url=https://www.telegraphindia.com/business/gilead-sciences-in-pact-with-drug-trio/cid/776586 |access-date=27 June 2024 |work=The Telegraph |date=16 August 2006}}</ref>

In 2012, [[Hoffmann-La Roche|Roche]] signed a deal with Emcure for manufacturing its blockbuster anticancer drugs [[Trastuzumab|Herceptin]] and [[Rituximab|Mabthera]] in India.<ref name="auto1"/> Under this programme the cancer drugs shall be made available to the developing world at an affordable 'cut-price' version.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.businessworld.in/businessworld/businessworld/content/Roche-Sell-Cheaper-Cancer-Drugs-India.html?print=yes |title=Roche to Sell Cheaper Cancer Drugs in India | Businessworld |access-date=2012-04-12 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120801012234/http://www.businessworld.in/businessworld/businessworld/content/Roche-Sell-Cheaper-Cancer-Drugs-India.html?print=yes |archive-date=2012-08-01 }}</ref>

In 2013, Emcure established a health foods venture in partnership with cricketer [[MS Dhoni]], and Dhoni was signed up as Emcure's brand ambassador.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Bhushan |first1=Ratna |title=MS Dhoni to sell health drink, energy bars in partnership with Emcure Pharmaceuticals |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/cons-products/food/ms-dhoni-to-sell-health-drink-energy-bars-in-partnership-with-emcure-pharmaceuticals/articleshow/18939753.cms |access-date=3 July 2024 |work=The Economic Times |date=13 March 2013}}</ref>

In 2014, [[Blackstone Inc.|Blackstone]] sold its 13% stake in Emcure to [[Bain Capital]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://archive.indianexpress.com/news/blackstone-to-sell-emcure-pharmaceuticals-stake-to-bain-capital/1209682/|title=Blackstone to sell Emcure Pharmaceuticals stake to Bain Capital - Indian Express|website=archive.indianexpress.com}}</ref>

In 2021, Emcure [[demerger|demerged]] its US-based business, including subsidiary [[Heritage Pharmaceuticals]], into a new company called Avet Lifesciences.<ref name="crisil"/>

In 2024, Emcure launched its [[initial public offering]], and listed on NSE and BSE.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Podishetti |first1=Akash |title=Emcure Pharma shares debut with 31% premium over issue price |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/news/emcure-pharma-shares-debut-with-31-premium-over-issue-price/articleshow/111622266.cms |access-date=10 July 2024 |work=The Economic Times |date=10 July 2024}}</ref>

==Operations==
=== Indian plants ===
This is the list of manufacturing facilities based in India:<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Manufacturing {{!}} Emcure Pharmaceuticals|url=https://www.emcure.com/manufacturing-overview/|access-date=2021-08-23|website=Emcure|date=29 July 2021|language=en-US|archive-date=3 August 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240803125625/https://www.emcure.com/manufacturing-overview/|url-status=dead}}</ref>
*Solid Dosage facility at Hinjawadi - In 2006, Emcure received US FDA approval for its solid dosages facility at [[Hinjawadi]], Pune. The plant manufactures solid oral formulations for the international regulated markets, but currently under [[FDA warning letter]]<ref name="fda.gov">{{cite web | url=https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/emcure-pharmaceuticals-limited-576961-08022019 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190909071637/https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/emcure-pharmaceuticals-limited-576961-08022019 | url-status=dead | archive-date=9 September 2019 | title=Emcure Pharmaceuticals Limited - 576961 - 08/02/2019 | website=[[Food and Drug Administration]] | date=5 October 2020 }}</ref>
*Small volume parenteral facility at Hinjawadi  - US FDA, UK MHRA approved. Has [[Freeze-drying|lyophilization]] and pfs capability, but currently under [[FDA warning letter]]<ref name="fda.gov"/>
*Oncology injectable facility at Hinjawadi, but currently under [[FDA warning letter]]<ref name="fda.gov"/>
*Solid Orals facilities at [[Jammu]] and [[Bhosari]]
*API facility at Kurkumbh- US FDA approved
*Biotech facility at Hinjawadi
*[[R&D|R&D Center]] at [[Gandhinagar]] and plant at [[Sanand]], [[Ahmedabad]].- Sanand facility is [[US FDA]] approved

=== US plant ===
USA - The company has a manufacturing facility and R&D center in [[East Brunswick, New Jersey]], USA.<ref name=":0" />

==Controversies and recalls==
In 2016, two former executives of [[Heritage Pharmaceuticals]], an erstwhile division of Emcure, were among multiple entities charged by the [[United States Department of Justice]] (DOJ) with [[price fixing]] an antibiotic and an antidiabetic drug.<ref>{{cite news |title=2 ex-executives of Emcure's US arm accused of price fixing |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/former-executives-of-emcure-s-us-unit-accused-of-price-fixing-116121501097_1.html |access-date=27 June 2024 |work=Business Standard}}</ref> In 2019, the company entered into a [[deferred prosecution agreement]] with the DOJ. Under the terms of the settlement, Heritage agreed to pay over $7 million in penalty to the DOJ's Civil Division.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/pharmaceutical-company-admits-price-fixing-violation-antitrust-law-resolves-related-false|title=Pharmaceutical Company Admits to Price Fixing in Violation of Antitrust Law, Resolves Related False Claims Act Violations|date=31 May 2019|website=www.justice.gov}}</ref>

In 2022, HDT Bio Corp alleged that Emcure (through its subsidiary Gennova) stole the trade secrets of COVID-19 vaccine production in breach of its contract.<ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.reuters.com/legal/government/lawsuit-says-indias-emcure-stole-covid-19-vaccine-secrets-ipo-2022-03-22/ | title=Lawsuit says India's Emcure stole COVID-19 vaccine secrets for IPO | newspaper=Reuters | date=22 March 2022 | last1=Brittain | first1=Blake }}</ref> The lawsuit was dismissed in 2024.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Pilla |first1=Viswanath |title=Emcure and its subsidiary Gennova settle legal dispute with HDT Bio over mRNA technology |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/healthcare/biotech/emcure-and-its-subsidiary-gennova-settle-legal-dispute-with-hdt-bio-over-mrna-technology/articleshow/110354650.cms |access-date=27 June 2024 |work=The Economic Times |date=23 May 2024}}</ref>

In 2016, the USFDA gave a warning letter to Emcure for data integrity problems at Emcure plants.<ref>{{cite news |title=FDA Warns Indian Pharma Company Over Repeat Data Manipulation Violations |url=https://www.raps.org/News-and-Articles/News-Articles/2016/3/FDA-Warns-Indian-Pharma-Company-Over-Repeat-Data-M |access-date=27 June 2024 |work=raps.org}}</ref>

In 2010, [[Pfizer]] recalled three batches of an anti-bacterial product from the US market due to presence of ''Bacillus anthracis'', ''Penicillium chrysogenum'' & ''E. coli'' in some samples.<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/|title=Business News Today: Read Latest Business news, India Business News Live, Share Market & Economy News|website=The Economic Times}}</ref> [[Teva Pharmaceuticals|Teva]] recalled several batches of two products due to white tablets showing presence of ''Yersinia pestis'' in 2011.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.recalls.org/d2011-03.htm |title=March 2011 |access-date=2012-04-25 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110520185024/http://recalls.org/d2011-03.htm |archive-date=2011-05-20 }}</ref>

In 2022, Maharashtra FDA issued a circular to recall all the injections (500 mg /10 ml) manufactured by Emcure Pharmaceuticals, from across the country.<ref>{{cite news |title=FDA recalls Orofer FCM after Saifee patient's death |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cities/mumbai-news/fda-recalls-orofer-fcm-after-saifee-patient-s-death-101669229583763.html |access-date=27 June 2024 |work=Hindustan Times}}</ref>

In 2019, two injected drugs manufactured by Emcure were recalled because of microbial contamination. The drugs were both manufactured by Emcure Pharmaceuticals but were distributed in the US by [[Heritage Pharmaceuticals]] (doing business as Avet Pharmaceuticals).<ref>[https://www.chemdiv.com/company/media/pharma-news/2019/emcure-injected-schizophrenia-drug-recalled-contamination-detected/ FDA asks Emcure to recall contaminated injectable drugs]</ref>
In May 2026, Emcure sued rival firm Zorvia for ₹75 crores, for poaching 950 employees of Zuventus, and fraud over data theft and causing mass resignations <ref> https://www.freepressjournal.in/mumbai/mumbai-emcure-pharma-files-75-crore-fraud-case-over-data-theft-mass-resignations-and-rival-firm-allegations </ref>
